evidence_class: model review (GPT-6 astra at effort max over each card's retained sources): judgment, not execution; findings are claims to verify, not acceptance

reviews.summary: The native scoped archive/CLI lane is supported and runnable, but installed 0.43.0 trails the published 0.44.0 successor and default worker-history coverage remains incomplete (groups/g6-docs-accounting/agentsview.upstream.json; https://github.com/kenn-io/agentsview/releases/tag/v0.44.0). There is no exact token-efficiency comparison or native saved-token counter, so comparison eligibility and attributable savings are unverified; the retained benefit is successful post-start project reads and one selected Claude plus one selected Codex session returned with inclusive flags (cards/agentsview.json; ../rr/returned-results.json#agentsview-11-projects-daemon; ../rr/returned-results.json#agentsview-15-session-list-claude-inclusive; ../rr/returned-results.json#agentsview-16-session-list-codex-inclusive). The pre-start refusals are explained by disabled daemon autostart, while later empty lists are explained by default one-shot exclusion, and all four historical verifier findings were already dispositioned at assembly (../rr/returned-results.json#components/agentsview). The 36-hour scan ending 2026-09-26T23:37:28Z detects use by 32/1010 Ultracode workflow children (3.17%, 238 CLI detections), 1/301 Codex workers (0.33%, 11), and 1/22 children given the lanes block (4.55%, 1) (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, preserve the successful recovered records, document intended one-shot/automated/child coverage, and qualify the successor on a scoped archive copy before upgrading or claiming complete worker-history coverage.

Installed v2.4.1 matches the latest release, and explicit-scoped HTTP MCP plus allowlisted native hooks are supported upstream choices, but restricted-worker recall and portable hook wiring still have gaps. The retained Claude and host-policy Codex queries returned the same ten hits, but the baseline was deliberately empty and no exact savings comparison exists, so adapted token performance is unverified rather than zero or a pass (../rr/ai-memory/records.json#ai-memory-e2-codex-exec; evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-codex-20260926/receipt.json). Real Codex lifecycle capture after hook trust is proven separately, while PreCompact remains unverified and this restricted worker's recall probe was denied (evidence/artifacts/ai-memory-241-codex-capture-20260926/README.md; groups/final-verdict-evidence.json#live_probes). The fixed scan found invocations in 105/1,010 Ultracode children (10.40%) and 3/301 Codex workers (1.00%), including 4/22 TOKEN LANES children (18.18%); lifecycle capture is not added to these invocation counts (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, qualify recall under the intended restricted worker policy, render hook paths from each platform's installed version, correct stale trust/count summaries, and retain an actual PreCompact observation and a task-matched savings baseline.

The installed 0.45.3 CLI matches the latest published upstream release and the explicit structural-search lane is supported, but configuration guidance still needs the released-pin limitations recorded in groups/g5-conversion-packing/ast-grep.upstream.json. The card's historical Claude comparison is 105877→10293 tokens (90.28%) and its Codex comparison is 112899→11508 (89.81%); both eligibility fields are null, so these totals alone do not establish an eligible fidelity pass (cards/ast-grep.json). The separately retained call-extraction comparison is 133697→10903 o200k_base tokens (91.84%), eligible only for the checked subprocess-call task because all 19 call ranges and source slices agree with the Python AST oracle (../rr/ast-grep/out/17-compare.stdout; ../rr/ast-grep/check/check.json). The 36-hour scan ending 2026-09-26T23:37:28Z detects use by 44/1010 Ultracode workflow children (4.36%, 243 CLI detections), 2/301 Codex workers (0.66%, 7), and 0/22 children given the lanes block (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, document trusted configuration and original-source recovery, qualify the first release containing the existing opt-in fix, and measure successful use on eligible tasks; native saved-token counters and attributable provider savings remain unverified.

The installed 20.0.24 CLI matches the latest published release and the explicit native-history accounting lane is supported, including the intentional offline/no-cost Codex recipe (groups/g6-docs-accounting/ccusage.upstream.json; https://github.com/ccusage/ccusage/releases/tag/v20.0.24). No exact token-savings comparison or native saved-token counter is present, so savings eligibility remains unverified; the actual retained result is correct synthetic token accounting across 34 checks, with a deliberately changed input rejected by two checks (cards/ccusage.json; ../rr/ccusage/out/check-fixture.stdout; ../rr/ccusage/out/check-fixture-negative-control.stdout). The retained Claude report leaves claude-opus-5-5 unpriced and the Codex report flags gpt-6-luna while omitting cost fields under --no-cost, which is an offline-pricing coverage limit explained by upstream's embedded snapshot and configurable overrides (../rr/ccusage/out/claude-daily-before.stdout; ../rr/ccusage/out/codex-daily-before.stdout; https://github.com/ccusage/ccusage/blob/v20.0.24/docs/guide/config-files.md#pricing-overrides). The 36-hour scan ending 2026-09-26T23:37:28Z detects use by 63/1010 Ultracode workflow children (6.24%, 430 CLI detections), 1/301 Codex workers (0.33%, 1), and 1/22 children given the lanes block (4.55%, 9) (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, retain the token-only lane and qualify a separate pricing configuration when complete cost reporting is required; the five historical verifier findings already have assembly dispositions and are not unresolved savings defects.

Installed v0.11.0 matches the latest release and supports the chosen explicit-index graph workflow, but portable installation and Claude agent access remain incomplete. The historical verified task artifacts were 22,445→19,635 tokens for Claude (12.5%) and 22,445→16,109 for Codex (28.2%), eligible only for those checked caller-retrieval tasks, not provider savings (evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-ultracode-20260925/receipt.json; evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-codex-20260926/receipt.json). The newer MCPorter comparisons of 56,274→865 (98.5%) and 56,274→1,410 (97.5%) are not clean complete-answer savings: graph-only recall is 4/7, while search_code restores 7/7 recall but includes one false positive (../rr/codebase-memory-mcp/records.json#codebase-memory-mcp:compare-mcp-plan; #codebase-memory-mcp:compare-mcp-plan-plus-search-code). In the fixed 36-hour scan, 9/1,010 Ultracode workflow children (0.89%) and 1/301 Codex workers (0.33%) invoked it, with 0/22 children carrying TOKEN LANES invoking it; these are invocation observations, not success rates (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, qualify explicit indexing, source-validated fallback and narrow Claude grants, preserve low-confidence candidates for verification, and measure the intended native worker path without combining artifact counts with counters or provider usage.

The installed 0.1.4 CLI matches the latest published release and upstream's search-then-get workflow, but current CLI version does not guarantee current curated content (groups/g6-docs-accounting/context-hub.upstream.json). The historical Uvicorn fact comparison is 70903→2073 tokens (97.08%) with null card eligibility; separately, retained FastAPI CLI and MCP comparisons each reproduce 503515→3094 o200k_base tokens (99.39%), eligible only for the checked strict_content_type introduction fact and not for complete release coverage (cards/context-hub.json; ../rr/context-hub/out/23-o200k-compare-cli.stdout; ../rr/context-hub/out/24-o200k-compare-mcp.stdout; ../rr/context-hub/out/10-quality-check.stdout). The freshly fetched FastAPI document still declares version 0.136.3, while the retained stack target is 0.141.1 and that target is absent from the retrieved document (https://github.com/andrewyng/context-hub/blob/main/content/fastapi/docs/package/python/DOC.md; ../rr/context-hub/out/10-quality-check.stdout). The 36-hour scan ending 2026-09-26T23:37:28Z detects use by 8/1010 Ultracode workflow children (0.79%, 28 CLI detections), 1/301 Codex workers (0.33%, 6), and 0/22 children given the lanes block (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, gate retrieved documentation on the needed version and fact coverage, refresh cache when appropriate and fall back to current primary documentation; native saved-token counters and attributable provider savings remain unverified.

The installed npm version matches latest stable 1.0.169, but the source-justified session-bound Codex template is still unapplied on this host and npm version equality does not identify the separately installed plugin source (docs/decisions/2026-09-25-codex-mcp-scope.md:216; groups/verdict-evidence.json; https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/releases/tag/v1.0.169). Both historical lane comparisons are 97952→204 tokens (99.8%), eligible for the requested heading/count summary only; the separate returned-results top-ten-heading extraction is 97952→165 with its own passing check (../html-report/savings.json#report_comparisons; ../rr/context-mode/out/18-compare-execute-file.stdout; ../rr/context-mode/out/16-check-execute-file.stdout). The retained Claude 3244032 and Codex 6311424 saved-token snapshots are separately scoped event/byte estimates, not additional exact savings or avoided provider usage (../html-report/savings.json#native_snapshot). The scan labels 162/1010 Ultracode workflow children (16.04%, 2233 MCP and 125 CLI matches), 265/301 eligible Codex workers (88.04%, 5293 MCP and 2 CLI matches), and 21/22 workflow_children_with_lanes_block (95.45%) as users; the subgroup association is not causal evidence (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, adopt the reviewed launch binding, explicitly resolve the main-checkout exception, and verify real concurrent native sessions and worker access before declaring the host adaptation complete.

The fixed 3.4.0 o200k_base library is an appropriate native measurement dependency, but upstream latest is 4.0.0 and compatibility still needs qualification (tools/token-report/token_manifest.py:159; https://github.com/niieani/gpt-tokenizer/releases/tag/4.0.0). No eligible reduction comparison measures savings produced by the tokenizer itself; the 22 freshly recounted artifacts support other tools' comparisons, with provider savings unverified (groups/verdict-evidence.json; cards/gpt-tokenizer.json#adapted_performance). The retained local cross-check reports 26/27 checks, and its follow-up finds ordinary-text agreement but special-token discrepancies in both 3.4.0 and 4.0.0, so upgrading alone does not resolve that boundary (../rr/gpt-tokenizer/out/36-crosscheck.stdout; ../rr/gpt-tokenizer/out/44-special-report.stdout). The retained invoke scan labels 45/1010 Ultracode workflow children (4.46%, 189 CLI matches), 1/301 eligible Codex workers (0.33%, 4 CLI matches), and 0/22 workflow_children_with_lanes_block as users; these are command-text observations, not successful-call or opportunity rates (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, qualify the actual callers against 4.0.0 and make ordinary-text versus special-token acceptance explicit while preserving reproducible measurement provenance.

On-demand MCP compression and retrieval are upstream-supported, but this host retains 0.37.0 while latest is 0.39.1 and lacks two offline guards already present in its template (https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/v0.39.1/docs/content/docs/mcp.mdx; groups/verdict-evidence.json). Historical Claude 237691→56939 (76.0%) and Codex 210316→14611 (93.1%) comparisons measure selected compression responses with their recorded answer/recovery checks, not recovery-inclusive provider savings (../html-report/savings.json#report_comparisons). The separate retained fixture compresses body text 181298→13827 (92.4%) but compression plus full retrieval is 181298→195125 (+7.6%), so eligibility depends on the required information and recovery cost; the native counter remains a separate estimate (../rr/headroom/out/13-compare-compressed.stdout; ../rr/headroom/out/14-compare-recovery.stdout). The scan labels 58/1010 Ultracode workflow children (5.74%, 6 MCP and 135 CLI matches), 1/301 eligible Codex workers (0.33%, 3 MCP and 2 CLI matches), and 0/22 workflow_children_with_lanes_block as users (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, qualify 0.39.1 against the retained omission-count and recovery cases, reconcile the host guards and complete target selection, and measure useful compression including any retrieval.

Installed v1.108.319 matches the latest release, and the pinned executable with selected indexing fits upstream guidance; project-only registration is an intentional local routing choice that still leaves fresh worktrees without the server. The newer source-verified comparison is 25,440→570 o200k_base tokens (97.8%), eligible for MCPorter-rendered search_symbols plus get_symbol_source against a whole-file baseline, with the one-time index response excluded and native-client rendering unmeasured (../rr/jcodemunch-mcp/records.json#jcodemunch-mcp-74-compare-retrieval). The historical native Claude result is separately 22,043→443 (98.0%), while the newer +27,267 native ledger delta is an estimate rather than the exact 24,870-token artifact reduction; no successful fresh-worktree Codex comparison is available (evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-ultracode-20260925/receipt.json; evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-codex-20260926/receipt.json; ../rr/jcodemunch-mcp/records.json#jcodemunch-mcp-14-counter-after). The fixed scan found invocations in 64/1,010 Ultracode children (6.34%) and 3/301 Codex workers (1.00%), including 1/22 TOKEN LANES children (4.55%); invocation does not establish successful retrieval (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, render and verify the project entry in each opted-in worktree, correct the conflicting copyable recipe, and retain a successful native Codex task before claiming equivalent worker performance.

The installed 0.1.8 base CLI matches the latest release and upstream permits selecting format dependencies, so the native HTML lane is aligned while fresh-bootstrap equivalence remains unqualified (groups/g5-conversion-packing/markitdown.upstream.json). The historical card comparisons are 503230→28934 tokens (94.25%) for Claude and 505768→29471 (94.17%) for Codex, with null eligibility fields rather than an explicit acceptance decision (cards/markitdown.json). The separately retained HTML comparison is 33177→2556 o200k_base tokens (92.30%), eligible for recovering the checked market-hours fact and 14 additional visible facts, not arbitrary document fidelity (../rr/markitdown/out/10-o200k-compare.stdout; ../rr/markitdown/out/7-quality-check.stdout). The 36-hour scan ending 2026-09-26T23:37:28Z detects use by 67/1010 Ultracode workflow children (6.63%, 517 CLI detections), 1/301 Codex workers (0.33%, 4), and 0/22 children given the lanes block (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, run the unperformed clean-install promotion gate and enforce input-format and required-content checks; PDF/Office/OCR coverage, native savings counters and attributable provider savings remain unverified.

For its selected Linux CLI-bridge role, installed MCPorter 0.14.1 matches latest stable and the supported upstream architecture; the retained qualification reports 37/37 checks on both candidate and baseline (https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/releases/tag/v0.14.1; evidence/receipts/mcporter-0141-qualification-20260925.json). There is no eligible standalone token-reduction comparison or native savings counter: returned-results demonstrate transport and exact cross-process recovery, while attributable token savings remain unverified (cards/mcporter.json#adapted_performance; ../rr/returned-results.json#components/mcporter). The failed shared Headroom call omitted --server, and its corrected invocation succeeds with file-backed content, matching upstream selector parsing and key=@path support (../rr/returned-results.json#headroom-e2e-06-compress-attempt1-failed; #headroom-e2e-06-compress; https://github.com/openclaw/mcporter/blob/v0.14.1/docs/cli-reference.md). The scan labels 111/1010 Ultracode workflow children (10.99%, 1111 CLI matches), 2/301 eligible Codex workers (0.66%, 2 CLI matches), and 0/22 workflow_children_with_lanes_block as users; zero MCP calls is consistent with the selected CLI bridge and direct native server registrations (invoke_by_tool.json; docs/token-session-handbook.md:142). Next, standardize complete selectors for recurring workflows, preserve Node/ps and daemon-version checks, and measure successful useful calls without assigning downstream compression savings to the bridge.

Installed v2.8.3 matches the latest release, and standalone named-index MCP is supported, but the native catalog covers selected US-equities documents rather than the repository's adoption instructions. The true eligible isolated CLI comparison is 4,373→1,850 o200k_base tokens (57.7%) for search plus a source-verified window; the separate native Claude positive control is 5,756→3,367 (41.5%), while whole-document retrieval and search-plus-whole expand output by 0.3% and 16.9% respectively (../rr/qmd/records.json#qmd-compare-B-search-plus-window; #qmd-compare-D-claude-control; #qmd-compare-A-get-whole; #qmd-compare-C-search-plus-whole). The historical 5,756→901 claim (84.3%) is ineligible because it answered from the wrong document, and neither later valid comparison repairs that task failure or proves provider savings (evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-codex-20260926/receipt.json#corrections_to_296). The fixed scan found invocations in 64/1,010 Ultracode children (6.34%) and 11/301 Codex workers (3.65%), including 2/22 TOKEN LANES children (9.09%); this pass also confirmed a 122-document lexical catalog and used query then bounded get (invoke_by_tool.json; groups/final-verdict-evidence.json#live_probes). Next, check collection coverage before routing, use typed lex queries with rerank:false and bounded get, add refresh guards, and repair the card's stale PASS/count fields while retaining the named-index registration.

The installed 1.18.1 CLI matches the latest release and explicit-file packing is upstream-supported, but our use of compressed Python packs for complete definition lookup exceeds the verified fidelity (groups/g5-conversion-packing/repomix.upstream.json). The historical 17935→8799 o200k_base comparison (50.94%) is explicitly retracted for eligibility, and the newer CLI 23638→10565 (55.31%) and MCP 18641→8981 (51.82%) reductions are also ineligible for the complete-definition task because status_body and inspect definitions are missing (cards/repomix.json; ../rr/repomix/out/16-compare-cli.stdout; ../rr/repomix/out/17-compare-mcp.stdout; ../rr/repomix/check/def_names.json). The upstream pinned Python parser matches a signature only on its first line, which explains the multiline omission and calls for a local routing and acceptance fix (https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix/blob/v1.18.1/src/core/treeSitter/parseStrategies/PythonParseStrategy.ts#L81). The 36-hour scan ending 2026-09-26T23:37:28Z detects use by 55/1010 Ultracode workflow children (5.45%, 345 CLI detections), 2/301 Codex workers (0.66%, 7), and 0/22 children given the lanes block (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, use uncompressed selected files or explicit original-source recovery for exact definitions, replace the superseded PASS wording, and remeasure the complete workflow; native counters and attributable provider savings remain unverified.

Installed RTK 0.50.0 matches latest stable; Claude's hook with exactness exclusions and deliberate manual Codex use are supported adaptations, but upstream 0.50.0 also offers a Codex hook that this stack has not qualified (recipes/README.md:143; https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/blob/v0.50.0/hooks/codex/README.md). Historical answer-checked fixtures reduce Claude output 29986→3786 tokens (87.4%) and Codex output 25386→4278 (83.1%), eligible only for their selected information contracts (../html-report/savings.json#report_comparisons). The newer primary pair is 52009→50063 (3.7%) with recall needed for complete filenames and metadata still absent, while supplementary 44522→7130 (84.0%) excludes recall and truncates content; the separate native Codex pair 356→341 (4.2%) is explicitly lossy at 7/10 commit subjects (../rr/returned-results.json#rtk-L02-compare-primary; #rtk-L03-compare-supplementary; #codex-34-o200k-compare). The retained scan labels 192/1010 Ultracode workflow children (19.01%, 1454 CLI matches), 150/301 eligible Codex workers (49.83%, 1129 CLI matches), and 10/22 workflow_children_with_lanes_block (45.45%) as users (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, make exactness-aware guidance explicit, preserve raw recovery, qualify the Codex hook locally if selected, and remove unsupported causal explanations rather than treating fixture reductions or native counters as provider savings.

The immutable 2.0.0.dev0 development pin uses upstream's client-specific contexts and project binding; v1.7.0 remains the latest stable release, so replacing the development pin with it would not be a straightforward upgrade. The newer verified comparison is 25,942→2,168 o200k_base tokens (91.6%), eligible for the retained Python definition-and-reference fixture through MCPorter, with byte-identical Claude-context and Codex-context output and all 16 calls plus two import references preserved (../rr/serena/records.json#serena-20-o200k-compare; #serena-19-quality-check). Historical native-client comparisons remain separate at 17,723→1,752 for Claude (90.1%) and 22,445→7,810 for Codex (65.2%), and none proves provider savings or general language coverage (evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-ultracode-20260925/receipt.json; evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-codex-20260926/receipt.json). The fixed scan found 37/1,010 Ultracode children (3.66%) and 21/301 Codex workers (6.98%) invoking Serena, with 1/22 TOKEN LANES children (4.55%); this pass's initialization and targeted find_symbol both timed out and supply no new successful retrieval (invoke_by_tool.json; groups/final-verdict-evidence.json#live_probes). Next, investigate that live timeout without assuming its cause, reconcile user-scope startup settings, and qualify upstream's optional Claude and Codex reminder hooks against the existing retrieval lanes.

The pinned standalone 1.14.0 engine uses supported external Qdrant and an OpenAI-compatible embedding adapter; upstream's latest release is 1.15.0, already locally qualified but held for a coordinated cutover no earlier than 2026-10-01T11:01Z. The newer eligible source-verified native comparisons are 16,096→2,352 o200k_base tokens for Claude (85.4%) and 16,096→2,396 for Codex (85.1%), using five unfiltered hits for the host-request trust task (../rr/socraticode/records.json#socraticode-30-exact-o200k-comparisons; #socraticode-29-quality-checks). The historical 70.0% Claude and 90.6% Codex results use different result limits or file filtering and remain separate task-local artifact measurements, not provider savings (evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-ultracode-20260925/receipt.json; evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-codex-20260926/receipt.json). The fixed scan found invocations in 96/1,010 Ultracode children (9.50%) and 11/301 Codex workers (3.65%), including 2/22 TOKEN LANES children (9.09%); this restricted worker's health/status probe was denied and adds no successful native observation (invoke_by_tool.json; groups/final-verdict-evidence.json#live_probes). Next, follow the recorded cutover gate, reconcile user-scope startup timeout and intended Claude project registration, and verify explicit projectPath, index coverage, and native-client retrieval after the coordinated restart.

Installed TOON 4.1.1 is current and the selective CLI conversion with compact-JSON fallback matches upstream practice, but strict decoding alone does not guarantee value preservation (https://github.com/toon-format/toon/releases/tag/v4.1.1; https://github.com/toon-format/toon/blob/v4.1.1/packages/cli/README.md). The eligible 60-row uniform-table comparisons are 1642→907 o200k_base tokens (44.8%) in both Claude and Codex, whereas the nested catalog is 121472→132861 (+9.4%) and is ineligible as a saving, so compact JSON should be retained (../html-report/savings.json#report_comparisons). A separate two-row comparison saves 29→22 (24.1%), refuting an upstream five-row minimum, while a fresh installed-version check strictly decodes a BOM-prefixed string into a boolean (../rr/toon/out/12-stack-compare-o200k.sanitized.stdout; groups/verdict-evidence.json#toon_bom_check). The retained scan labels 62/1010 Ultracode workflow children (6.14%, 308 CLI matches), 3/301 eligible Codex workers (1.00%, 10 CLI matches), and 0/22 workflow_children_with_lanes_block as users; it does not count suitable conversion opportunities (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, replace the unqualified size heuristic with measured compact-JSON comparison and semantic round-trip checks, including the BOM case, before expanding use.

final-verdict-evidence.scope: Final verdict verification; scratch paths are relative to the token-cards directory, and adoption/docs/evidence paths are relative to the native stack repository. No installation or upstream issue changes were made.

recounts.method: Read the exact content-addressed baseline and candidate files referenced by retained comparison outputs; recompute SHA-256, byte size, and o200k_base tokens using the installed gpt-tokenizer module. Counts do not establish semantic eligibility.

q3.method: Opened the matching retained codebase-memory SQLite graph read-only, joined inbound CALLS edges to scripts/host_receipts.py register_file, and compared (file,name) pairs with ../cbm-q3/truth.json; opened original clone source to confirm the two low-confidence calls.

qmd.query_then_get: Completed typed lexical query with rerank:false and an eight-line get; returned document was a US-equities catalog, not the token-session handbook. No new savings measurement.

ai-memory.error: MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never

socraticode.error: MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never

invoke_scan.interpretation: Counts of detected invocation attempts and agents invoking; not tool-success rates, not causal savings, and not added to the separate OTel window.

g5-g6-verification.scope: Read-only final-verdict verification for g5-conversion-packing and g6-docs-accounting. Local evidence references are relative to token-cards, except docs/, recipes/ and evidence/ references, which are relative to the native stack repository. No installation, configuration, source card or upstream issue was changed.
g5-g6-verification.release_method: Fresh official /repos/<repository>/releases/latest API reads, corroborated by official release-page and documentation research; all reported releases are non-prereleases. Search-engine snippets were not used to override fresh release evidence.

attachment_check.method: Opened every attachment on every record naming the component and checked retained byte size and SHA-256. Counts are attachment references and may include the same file more than once; record status is not inferred from attachment integrity.

g5-g6-verification.recount_method: Opened the exact baseline and candidate files referenced by the native report ledger and retained comparison outputs, verified size and SHA-256, and recomputed o200k_base with the configured gpt-tokenizer module. Thirteen comparisons and 26 artifact checks reproduced with zero mismatches. Numeric reproduction alone does not establish semantic eligibility.

ast-grep-calls.eligibility: bounded subprocess-call extraction; 19 ranges match Python AST; all 15 checks pass

ast-grep-outline.eligibility: two-file top-level outline only; all six checks pass

markitdown-html.eligibility: bounded market-hours fact; required checks and 14 informative visible facts pass

context-hub-cli.eligibility: strict_content_type introduction fact only; primary check and discrimination control pass

context-hub-mcp.eligibility: same bounded fact and CLI-document parity; not additional savings

invoke_scan.interpretation: Reported command-text/MCP-name detections and agents detected, not successful execution or task-eligible adoption rates. Regex matches can include tool-name mentions inside command text. Existing frozen-window scan was inspected and cross-checked, not rerun over private transcripts. No sums across populations, OTel, native counters or provider usage.

review_resolutions.ast_grep: Corrected before/after-full-parsing wording read with the cited merged upstream sources.
review_resolutions.repomix: Stale historical PASS remains in payload; explicit eligibility retraction is present.
review_resolutions.agentsview: All four historical raw-record findings dispositioned; successful post-start projects and inclusive lists retained.
review_resolutions.ccusage: All five historical raw-record findings dispositioned; pricing gap remains.

g5-g6-verification.measurement_limits: No card provides a native saved-token counter; AgentsView and ccusage have no exact comparison. No attributable provider-savings measurement is established for any of the six. The retained fidelity checks were opened and assessed, not rerun as fresh application tests.
tool_limits: GitHub CLI authentication unavailable; public official web/API sources were used.
QMD query found no matching handbook entry in its active collections; original local handbook was opened.
Serena find_symbol failed because its language-server manager was uninitialized; the scanner source was opened directly and Serena configuration was not changed.

verdict-evidence.scope: Final-verdict read-only verification; locally authored summary of actual returned checks, not a new provider run or an unchanged upstream test suite.
verdict-evidence.path_convention: cards/, groups/, invoke_by_tool.json and ../rr or ../html-report paths are relative to token-cards; docs/, recipes/, tools/, adoption/ and evidence/ paths are relative to the main repository. Record names after # identify retained entries, not personal identifiers.
verdict-evidence.version_checks: Native --version for rtk, toon, headroom and mcporter; installed package.json for gpt-tokenizer and context-mode.
verdict-evidence.release_method: Fresh official GitHub releases/latest API responses (all HTTP 200), followed by opened official release pages and release/current upstream documentation; search-index snippets were not used as freshness authority.

retained_attachment_check.selection: All records whose component_ids include one of the six verdict tools, unique attachment paths.

historical_comparison_recount.method: Opened the private ledger's retained baseline/candidate paths, checked bytes and SHA256, then re-encoded fatal UTF-8 with installed gpt-tokenizer 3.4.0 cjs/encoding/o200k_base.js; private paths and ledger IDs omitted.
historical_comparison_recount.limit: A matching count and hash does not independently establish semantic acceptance; eligibility comes from each retained boundary and check.
